author: Mark Atwood
text:
Workspace-API consistency: SIGNIFICANT-DRIFT — the worst-divergence cluster is the extension *-types crates around capability surface (mail-types and chat-types both lack capability struct + URI const while the other 6 type crates expose them) and filter typing (chat-types is alone in using serde_json::Value for filter/comparator while all 7 siblings expose typed FilterCondition structs). These two gaps in the two most-mature workspace extensions force consumers to hardcode URI strings (mail-client does so 10+ times) and to interpret query filters as untyped JSON (chat-server). Secondary drift sits in the per-crate naming choices that escape the cookie-cutter template: tasks-client takes self by value instead of &self, filenode-client mixes three casings of FileNode in its own surface, and calendars-server has the only handler-fn naming outlier in 96 handlers.

The error-type and newtype surfaces are mostly small but real: CollisionError missing #[non_exhaustive] is a future-compat trap, and tasks-types using bare String for min/maxDateTime while calendars-types uses UTCDate for the same wire shape is preventable type-system loss.

Feature-flag drift (realistic-demo-ids absent from filenode-server) is benign at runtime but breaks test-fixture composability across the workspace.

Total: 15 P1-P3 findings filed. None P0 — no security-relevant trait-shape divergences observed (all 8 server backends use Self::Error wrapping, all 8 client crates use jmap_base_client::ClientError, none has fail-open vs fail-closed asymmetry visible from the public surface alone).
